sentences.text: The specific epithet cliftii commemorates William Clift, who served as curator of the Hunterian Museum.
Rexarthuria represents a newly proposed genus and a new taxonomic combination.
Only a single species, Rexarthuria cliftii, is currently assigned to the genus.
The species was first described within the genus Palaeornis, a name later found to be preoccupied by a bird and therefore invalid for this reptile.
Rexarthuria lived in the Early Cretaceous, specifically during the Valanginian age.
Its type locality is the Tunbridge Wells Sand Formation in England.
Fossils of the taxon have been recovered from the upper part of that formation.
Witton and colleagues re-examined the specimen in 2009 and argued it belongs to the lonchodectid group rather than the ornithocheirids.
A 2025 analysis by Thomas and McDavid placed the taxon as a sister group to the Tapejaridae.
Earlier assessments by Averianov in 2012 and 2014 referred the material to an indeterminate position within the broader Azhdarchoidea.
